spotlight.title: V2 budget is buying the wrong ads — fix the allocation, don't just watch it
spotlight.detail: Two days running, the four new V2 creatives have barely spent: "8 cups" and "captive agent" sit at $0.00 total. Yesterday's $5.76–$13.68 went 81% to "honest broker" — an old V1 ad, not the test you're trying to read — and "honest broker - Copy" is still rejected by Meta and hasn't been fixed or deleted. Day 6 of 10, $68.75 of $200 spent, and most of it isn't buying the experiment you think it is. Decide today: fix delivery on the new ads or call the test now, before the back half repeats the front half.

spotlight.title: The Sep 6 lead is still lost — four days, ten-plus alerts, same unfixed wire
spotlight.detail: Meta has counted 3 leads since Sep 5; only 2 ever reached the inbox. The missing one is from the newest ad, "Gap math new," and the watchdog's diagnosis hasn't changed since it was first narrowed: the V3 lead form is almost certainly not connected to the "Meta $300 Plan Leads" Google Sheet. This is a five-minute check that has now been repeated in at least ten separate watchdog emails since Sep 7 — the reporting loop works, the fixing loop doesn't. Wire it and prove it with one real submit today.

spotlight.title: Frankie's own test just found bug #2: leads that DO land get no welcome email
spotlight.detail: Overnight, Frankie ran an end-to-end test on his own email — lead "AMANDA" (L-YTCLT0-XC) reached the CRM cleanly at 04:31:59Z, but the W1 workflow never fired the welcome email, and the lead SLA-breached at 83 minutes untouched. This is a different failure from the Sep 6 lead: that one never reached the pipeline at all; this one reached it and the pipeline still dropped it. Two independent break points now confirmed in the same funnel. Fix the welcome-email step and re-submit to prove it, the same way you'll prove the sheet fix.
